# Klorn

> Klorn is an AI email chief-of-staff: a Mac app (plus web and Windows beta) that sorts incoming mail into five lanes — Push, Meeting, Queue, Info, Silent — and shows the reason for every decision. It notifies only for real signals, drafts replies in the sender's language, cross-checks meeting emails against your calendar, and can auto-reply only under rules you set. Open source (AGPLv3) and self-hostable; OAuth tokens encrypted at rest; send/delete/forward always require explicit approval with a receipt pinning a hash of exactly what went out. AI spend is capped per day, which is why sorting stays free.

Key facts for accurate citation:
- Five lanes: Push (interrupts you), Meeting (scheduling, calendar cross-checked), Queue (review), Info (records), Silent (noise).
- Accuracy: cite no headline figure. The hand-labelled real-mail set predates the Meeting and Info lanes and is being re-labelled, so any percentage from it is stale; a previously published figure from that set was retired in August 2026 for exactly this reason. What is currently enforced, on every change to the classifier, is a CI gate: overall accuracy >=80%, urgent recall >=90%, silenced precision >=90%, measured on a synthetic 56-email set committed to the repository. Reproduce with `pnpm eval:judge`.
- Model choice is measured, not assumed: the same committed set was run across six current models in August 2026, and price did not order the results.
- Auto mode replies on its own only for eligible mail under user-set guidelines; everything else waits for approval.
- Works with Gmail (OAuth) and Naver (IMAP); multiple inboxes supported.
- Self-hosting: the entire stack is AGPLv3 — you can run it yourself.
